sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Montclair?
sections.html:
Montclair is an Essex County township of 6.24 square miles, and a sale there runs through the Building Department, the Tax Collector and the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages. The township does not demand a new certificate of occupancy for a sale, but open permits and violations must be closed before closing.

This page walks through the Montclair numbers, the local paperwork, the 2026 tax bill and the three ways to sell: list with an agent, sell on your own, or take an as-is cash purchase.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Montclair homes?
sections.html:
Montclair is a high-value commuter market: the median owner-occupied home is worth $906,400, and more than half of households own. Population was 40,921 at the 2020 census and the Census Bureau estimates 44,633 for July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: How do Montclair's geography and neighborhoods affect a sale?
sections.html:
Montclair sits on the east face of First Mountain in the Watchung range, and from higher streets the New York skyline is about 12 miles away. The township was cut out of Bloomfield in 1868 so a second railroad could be built, became a town in 1894, and switched back to a township form of government in 1980.

Buyers shop by neighborhood and by train station. Named areas include Upper Montclair, Watchung Plaza, Church Street, Frog Hollow and South End, and the township has two ZIP Codes, 07042 and 07043. Six commercial districts anchor the blocks around them: Montclair Center around Six Corners, Upper Montclair, Watchung Plaza, Walnut Street, South End and Valley Road.

  • Montclair borders Bloomfield, Cedar Grove, Glen Ridge, Orange, Verona and West Orange in Essex County, plus Clifton and Little Falls in Passaic County.
  • Several brooks run east through town toward the Passaic River, so ask for any drainage or basement history in your disclosure notes.
  • Montclair Center won a national Great American Main Street Award in 2015, which buyers often mention when they describe the downtown.

sections.h2: Which trains, buses and schools matter to Montclair buyers?
sections.html:
Most Montclair buyers care first about the train. The Montclair-Boonton Line serves New York Penn Station and Hoboken Terminal, and seven NJ Transit stations serve the township: Bay Street, Walnut Street, Watchung Avenue, Upper Montclair, Mountain Avenue, Montclair Heights and Montclair State University. NJ Transit buses 11, 28, 29, 34, 97, 191 and 705 also run through town, most along Bloomfield Avenue.

Montclair Public Schools serve kindergarten through twelfth grade with seven elementary schools, three middle schools and Montclair High School, which had 1,961 students in 2022-23. The district as a whole enrolled 6,216 students. Montclair State University and private options such as Montclair Kimberley Academy also draw families, and listings usually name the elementary school zone.

sections.h2: Does Montclair require a certificate of occupancy to sell a house?
sections.html:
No. A June 2025 Building Department notice says the township does not require a new certificate of occupancy as a condition of a sale, mortgage or refinance. What it does require is that every current construction permit be closed and every open violation cleared before closing.

That rule is the real checkpoint for older houses with a finished attic, a new deck or a replaced boiler. The notice tells owners to pull the permit history through an Open Public Records Act request, then call the Building Department at 973-509-4951 to arrange closure. The office is on the second floor of the Municipal Building, 205 Claremont Avenue, and keeps weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Request the permit history before you list so a buyer's attorney does not find an open permit during attorney review.
  • If a second kitchen exists, expect to show a closed permit or a certificate of occupancy for it.
  • Landlords selling a rental should also ask the township's Rent Control Office what registration and notices apply.

sections.h2: How is a Montclair property tax bill set and when is it due?
sections.html:
Montclair taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Late interest runs 8% on the first $1,500 and 18% above that, counted from the first of the month.

The township's 2026 bill notice shows where the money goes. For an average home assessed at $641,700, the 2026 changes were about +$160.42 for the township, -$25.67 for Essex County and +$847.04 for the school budget. A voter-approved school referendum added $558.27 in 2026, with roughly the same amount billed in 2027. Montclair Public Schools take 54.25% of the levy, the township 23.72%, Essex County 14.53%, the Type I school district 2.90%, the referendum 2.32%, the library 1.57% and county open space 0.71%.

A buyer will ask for the current quarterly amount, so have the latest bill handy. At closing, the title company usually prorates the quarter in progress between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: Can I appeal my Montclair assessment?
sections.html:
Yes, but only the assessed value can be appealed, never the tax rate. The township's tax Q&A says a formal appeal must reach the Essex County Board of Taxation before May 1, and a Board decision can be taken to the New Jersey Tax Court within 45 days of notice.

Montclair also holds a tax sale once a year, and the buyer at that sale gets a lien certificate, not the deed. If any municipal charge or water and sewer balance is unpaid, clear it before you sign a contract so the title search comes back clean.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded and what transfer fees apply in Essex County?
sections.html:
An Essex County deed is recorded by the Register of Deeds and Mortgages, which keeps a copy of every deed and mortgage recorded since 1637 and serves all 22 county municipalities. Your closing attorney or title company normally files it.

The state's graduated fee applies to sales above $1 million, which matters in a town where the median home value is $906,400. For deeds submitted on or after July 10, 2025, the fee is a percentage of the full sale price: 1% when the price is over $1 million up to $2 million, 2% up to $2.5 million, 2.5% up to $3 million, 3% up to $3.5 million and 3.5% above that. It falls on the seller. Ask your attorney to run the figure before you accept an offer near those thresholds.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell on my own or take a cash offer in Montclair?
sections.html:
Each route trades price against time and effort. A listing can reach the most buyers in a market this strong, but it asks for repairs, staging and open permits closed up front. A cash buyer purchases as-is and can close on your schedule, which helps with inherited houses, tenant issues or a house with open permits.

  • Listing: highest potential price, longer timeline, showings and buyer financing contingencies.
  • Selling yourself: saves a commission but you handle pricing, disclosures and the contract with an attorney.
  • Cash purchase: as-is condition, flexible closing date, a lower price than a fully prepared listing.

Compare the net from each route after taxes, payoffs and the Building Department closeout. If you want a cash number for a Montclair house, you can request one without any obligation to accept it.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell in Montclair?
faqs.a: No. The township's Building Department says it does not require a new certificate of occupancy for a sale, mortgage or refinance. Open construction permits and violations must be closed before closing, and the Building Department at 973-509-4951 arranges the closeout.

faqs.q: When are Montclair property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Interest on late payments is 8% on the first $1,500 owed and 18% above that.

faqs.q: Where is a Montclair deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, which records property transactions for all 22 county municipalities. Your closing attorney or title agent usually submits the deed and the seller tax declaration.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Montclair house with open permits?
faqs.a: Yes, but the permits have to be closed before closing. Order the permit history through an Open Public Records Act request, then call the Building Department to schedule inspections or closeout. A cash buyer may take the work on, though the price will reflect it.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Montclair property assessment?
faqs.a: File with the Essex County Board of Taxation so the appeal arrives before May 1. If you disagree with the Board's decision, you can appeal to the New Jersey Tax Court within 45 days of notice. Only the assessment can be appealed, not the tax rate.
